lines.x: Doctor, where are you going? Shouldn't you be working? Lunch? Well then, I'm coming along. There's a few things I want to buy, and I can also keep a lookout for you.

Sorry, Doctor, Rhodes Island is just a part-time job for me. I have to study hard to make sure I have a nice, normal future ahead of me. If you plan to have me aboard and on 24-hour call… Well, I'll have to ask you reconsider that.

I color coded all the documents to be sent out, the backups have already been delivered, your schedule is right here. I bought your late night snack and put it in the refrigerator. Don't forget to heat it up. And last, oh, do you need me to change the light bulb in your office for you?

Did I ever tell you about my other job? No? Well, I won't. Don't look at me like that, Doctor. There's just not much to say. If my other office worked a tenth as hard as Rhodes Island does, they'd probably have become the only detective agency in Lungmen.

You wonder where I learned martial arts? Well, I have my old codger and his weird education to thank for that. Not that I resent kung fu. Martial arts should always be a part of me if I hope to uphold justice.

Just like how people value morality, martial arts have yin and yang, right and wrong. To right those wrongs, to defeat evil, to counter bad kung fu, these are all second nature to me. The world is dark, and someone must stand for justice.

You think you just saw me? In downtown Lungmen? That may have been me. I just finished class. Hm? You saw me beat down some thugs who were harassing a passerby? And then slipped away before the police arrived? Must have been someone else. Heh heh. Definitely. You were just seeing things, that's it.

My rotten dad said he had to go find the true meaning of kung fu before he went off, and I still don't know where he is. Please! What year does he think it is? Find some common sense and learn some responsibility before you get yourself killed. But at least I haven't forgotten what he taught me: 'Martial arts have martial virtue, humans have human kindness.'

Doctor, did any mail come for me? It did? Great. These are my grades... my very important grades! It's been straight A's for me, so far. If I don't work hard enough, I'll end up regretting all the things I wasn't strong enough to do.
Falling asleep at a time like this... Oh well, I'll just finish your work for you.
Is this Rhodes Island? Nice to meet you. I'm Waai Fu, your new part-timer. Please don't go easy on me. I can handle anything you ask of me. Yes, just give me the word.
If I can fight like this here, I can definitely knock them out.
Thank you very much, Doctor. You placed your trust in me, and I won't let you down.

I often witness injustices in my life. If I ever find myself unable to stop them, I reflect on the moment, and force myself to get stronger. So, if ever you need me, don't hesitate to say so. I'll be there, with all my strength!
More evil to fight against?
I have much to learn, but I won't turn down the responsibility.
Fight evil with the fist of justice!
Like cutting weeds and pulling roots!
Yes!
Go ahead!
A last resort.
All right!
You have crossed the line too far!
Pick on someone your own size!
Don't blink! Song Do Bart Cham style!
The mind directs, the fist executes!
Foul intentions lead a foul life. Repent now. There is still time.
A strong will conquers all.
That was not enough. I need to train more.
Father... I'm still... not strong enough.
At least it's better than some old, messy detective agency.
An ambush...?! ...Doctor, don't you ever sneak up on me like that again. Now let's get you to Medical first.
You want to go for a walk? Sure, let's get going. It's safer to have me with you.
Arknights.

Doctor, happy holidays. I—I was just taking a walk. I haven't had Hung's food in forever, so the moment I slip up... It really does take a strong will to resist temptation, I still need more training... Doctor, it's not too late yet. Let's go train together!
Care for some tea, Doctor?

Doctor, happy birthday to you! Please, take this present. It's a wooden dummy. 'When seeking the way, the greatest fear is to have no master nor opponent,' so to us who wish to be martial artists, it's both an opponent and a master. Alright, let me teach you how to train with it!

Working for Rhodes Island has been valuable practical experience for me. I've learned a great deal. But I think I need more experience still, before I can decide whether or not I should stay. Whatever the future brings, I believe you and I are fighting for justice.
